qualification.reason: This is an official Request for Quotations (RFQ) issued by NYS Office of General Services for an Aggregate Hardware Buy, including the solicitation for quotes, scope of work, submission deadlines, and evaluation criteria.

quotes.quote: RFQ Title Aggregate Hardware Buy 23-01 RFQ Number 23-01
Request for Quotations 23-01

OGS is seeking competitive quotes from Contract holders of the OGS Group 73600 Award 22802 Information Technology Umbrella Contract – Manufacturer Based (Statewide) (“Manufacturer Umbrella Contract”) for the Lot(s) indicated below.
BASIS FOR AWARD Highest Total Financial Score meeting specified Technical Requirements and Mandatory Pass/Fail Requirements for each Standard Configuration and associated Required Products.

OGS is releasing this Request for Quotes (RFQ) for Aggregate Hardware Buy 23-01 (“RFQ 23-01”).  The purpose of RFQ 23-01 is to establish an award for each Configuration as set forth in Attachment A - Technical Response.

findings.title: Discount Percentages Must Be Specific Values, Not Ranges
findings.fact: Discount percentage values cannot be expressed as a range (e.g., 10%-20% or 'varies').

quotes.quote: A Discount Percentage value cannot be expressed as a range (for example: 10%-20%, or “varies”).

findings.title: Quarterly Sales Report Submission Deadline
findings.fact: Sales reports are due to OGS one month after the end of each quarter.

quotes.quote: Sales reports are due to OGS one (1) month directly following the end of each quarter.

findings.title: Imaging Test Unit and Delivery Deadlines
findings.fact: Contractor shall provide a test unit with customized image within 5 business days of receiving the image, and deliver remainder of imaged units within 30 calendar days from written approval of test unit, but not less than 45 days from Purchase Order.

quotes.quote: If an Authorized User requires customized factory imaging, the Contractor shall provide a test unit with the customized image within five (5) business days of receiving the Authorized User’s image. The Contractor must deliver the remainder of the imaged units ordered by the Authorized User, within 30 calendar days from the date of Authorized User’s written approval of the test unit. Notwithstanding the foregoing in this clause the delivery date shall not be required to be less than 45 days from date of Purchase Order.

findings.title: Customer Service Response Time
findings.fact: Inquiries shall be responded to within twenty-four (24) hours.

quotes.quote: Inquiries shall be responded to within twenty-four (24) hours.

findings.title: Fiscal Audit Notice Period
findings.fact: OGS reserves the right to audit upon not less than 15 business days prior written notice.

quotes.quote: Audits shall be conducted during regular business hours, upon not less than 15 business days prior written notice.

findings.title: Stage 1 Administrative Review
findings.fact: Stage 1 reviews completeness of Attachment A, Attachment D, and Manufacturer Information page. Alterations to documents are prohibited and may result in rejection.

quotes.quote: The submitted Attachment A – Technical Response, Attachment D – Issue Escalation Plan, and the Manufacturer Information page (last page of this document) will be reviewed for completeness. The addition or deletion of worksheets, columns, unlocking the document, rewriting formulas, or similar alterations to any document is prohibited. OGS reserves the right to reject any RFQ Submission or portion(s) thereof determined to have been altered/modified by the Contractor from the original format. Failure to provide fully completed documents may result in rejection of the RFQ Submission without further review.

findings.title: Price Modification Procedures
findings.fact: Contractor can lower pricing of products at any time, but must follow specific procedures for adding or deleting products.

quotes.quote: All Product pricing on the Contractor’s Agreement price list can be lowered at any time throughout the term of any resulting Agreement and any extensions.

After Agreement award, in order for a Product to be added to the Additional Products pricing category under the Agreement, a Product must first be approved on the Contractor’s Manufacturer Umbrella Contract in accordance with the Contractor’s Manufacturer Umbrella Contract Appendix C – Contract Modification Procedure.

findings.title: Reseller Participation
findings.fact: Contractors may use Resellers for fulfillment, but must receive payment and invoice directly; Resellers are not authorized to receive Purchase Orders or invoice.

quotes.quote: Contractors are permitted to use Resellers in the fulfillment of orders under any resulting Agreement. Contractors must receive payment from Authorized Users directly and must invoice Authorized Users directly. OGS approved Resellers and Sales Agents are not authorized to receive Purchase Orders from Authorized Users or to invoice Authorized Users.

findings.title: Only Lot 2 Hardware Contractors Eligible
findings.fact: Only Contractors holding an award for Lot 2 – Hardware under the Manufacturer Umbrella Contract are eligible to bid; Resellers are not eligible and will be disqualified.
findings.business_implication: This RFQ is restricted to existing Lot 2 contract holders. Resellers or non-Lot 2 contractors cannot participate, and any bid from them will be rejected. This ensures that only qualified manufacturers or their authorized distributors with an existing state contract can compete.
findings.action_recommendation: Confirm that your company holds a valid Lot 2 – Hardware award under the Manufacturer Umbrella Contract before investing time in preparing a bid. If you are a reseller, do not attempt to bid as you will be disqualified. If you are a Lot 2 contractor, ensure your contract is active and in good standing.

quotes.quote: Quotes from Resellers will not be accepted. Contractors must have an award for Lot 2 to bid on this RFQ.

RFQ 23-01 is only being distributed to Contractors holding an award for Lot 2 – Hardware under the Manufacturer Umbrella Contract (“Contractors”). Quotes under RFQ 23-01 will only be accepted from Lot 2 Contractors on the Manufacturer Umbrella Contract; Resellers are not eligible to respond and any bids from a Reseller will be disqualified.

findings.title: Products Must Be on Manufacturer Umbrella Contract Price List
findings.fact: All proposed products (Standard Configuration, Required Products, Additional Products) must be on the Contractor's Manufacturer Umbrella Contract Lot 2 - Hardware price list at the time of the RFQ Submission due date.
findings.business_implication: The bidder can only offer products that are already listed on their approved Manufacturer Umbrella Contract price list. Any product not on the list at the submission deadline will be disqualified, potentially rendering the entire bid non-responsive. This limits the bidder's flexibility to introduce new products for this RFQ.
findings.action_recommendation: Review the current Manufacturer Umbrella Contract price list to ensure all products you intend to propose are listed. If any desired products are missing, submit a contract modification request well before the RFQ submission due date, indicating that the products are intended for RFQ 23-01. Verify that all SKUs are correctly listed and match the required configurations.

quotes.quote: All Products proposed as part of the Standard Configuration and Products proposed for Required Products, as well as any Additional Products, must be on the Contractor's Manufacturer Umbrella Contract Lot 2 - Hardware price list at the time of the RFQ Submission due date.
All proposed SKUs for Products offered must be on the Contractor’s approved Manufacturer Umbrella Contract price list prior to the RFQ Submission due date for RFQ 23-01.

findings.title: Bid Validity Period
findings.fact: Quotes and pricing must remain valid for at least 120 calendar days from the RFQ submission due date, unless extended by mutual consent.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must commit to holding their pricing and terms for a minimum of 120 days, which is longer than typical commercial bids. This could expose the bidder to market price fluctuations or cost increases during the evaluation period. However, it also demonstrates commitment and may be a factor in the award decision.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure that your pricing strategy accounts for potential cost changes over the 120-day validity period. Consider including contingency clauses or hedging strategies to mitigate risks. Be prepared to honor the quoted prices for the full validity period, and monitor market conditions to assess if an extension is needed.

quotes.quote: Quotes and pricing submitted in response to RFQ 23-01 must remain open and valid for at least 120 calendar days from the date that RFQ Submissions are due, unless the time for making an award is extended by mutual consent of OGS and the Contractor.

findings.title: No Exceptions to Appendix A and Material Terms
findings.fact: OGS will not entertain exceptions to Appendix A (Standard Clauses for New York State Contracts) or material exceptions to the RFQ or Appendix B.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must accept all terms in Appendix A and cannot propose material deviations from the RFQ or Appendix B. This means the bidder must comply with the state's standard contract clauses, which may include terms that are non-negotiable and potentially unfavorable. Any attempt to take exceptions could render the bid non-responsive.
findings.action_recommendation: Carefully review Appendix A and Appendix B to understand the mandatory terms. Ensure that your bid fully complies with these terms without proposing any exceptions. If you have concerns about specific clauses, address them during the question period, but be prepared that OGS will not entertain exceptions to Appendix A or material exceptions to the RFQ/Appendix B.

quotes.quote: Contractor is advised that OGS will not entertain any exceptions to Appendix A (Standard Clauses for New York State Contracts). OGS will also not entertain exceptions to the RFQ or Appendix B (General Specifications) that are of a material and substantive nature.

findings.title: Eligibility Restricted to Manufacturer Umbrella Contract Holders
findings.fact: Only Contractors with an approved Manufacturer Umbrella Contract can participate in RFQ 23-01, and all proposed products must be on the Contractor's approved Manufacturer Umbrella Contract price list.
findings.business_implication: This reinforces the strict eligibility criteria: only contractors with an approved Manufacturer Umbrella Contract can bid, and all products must be on their approved price list. This ensures that only pre-qualified vendors with established pricing are considered, reducing risk for OGS but limiting competition.
findings.action_recommendation: Verify that your company holds an approved Manufacturer Umbrella Contract and that all proposed products are listed on your approved price list. If you are not a contract holder, you cannot participate. If you are, ensure your contract is active and your price list is up-to-date before the submission deadline.

quotes.quote: All Additional Products proposed by a Contractor on Attachment A – Technical Response and Attachment C – Financial Response must first be on Contractor’s approved Manufacturer Umbrella Contract price list.

OGS reserves the right to decline to include any proposed Additional Product on any resulting awarded Configuration price list if not included on Contractor’s approved Manufacturer Umbrella Contract price list or if the proposed Additional Product is deemed to be out of scope for the Configuration by OGS.

findings.title: Exclusion of Entities on US Customs and Border Patrol Lists
findings.fact: OGS will not accept a bid from a Contractor or a Contractor Product that contains products made by an entity on any of the lists maintained by the US Customs and Border Patrol.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must ensure that all products offered, including those from suppliers, are not manufactured by entities on the US CBP withhold release orders and findings lists. Failure to comply will result in bid rejection and potential contract termination.
findings.action_recommendation: Conduct thorough due diligence on the entire supply chain to verify that no components or finished products originate from listed entities. Regularly monitor the CBP list and establish a compliance process to ensure ongoing adherence.

quotes.quote: OGS will not accept a bid from a Contractor, or a Contractor Product that contains Products made by an entity on any of the lists maintained by the US Customs and Border Patrol at the link set out below.

findings.title: EPEAT Certification Requirements for Desktops, Laptops, and Monitors
findings.fact: Desktops, laptops, and computer monitors must achieve EPEAT Gold certification at time of award, except Chromebooks which require EPEAT Silver.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must ensure that all offered desktops, laptops, and monitors meet the specified EPEAT certification levels. Failure to do so will result in disqualification. This may limit product options and require sourcing from manufacturers with certified products.
findings.action_recommendation: Verify EPEAT certification status for all proposed products and ensure they meet the required levels (Gold for most, Silver for Chromebooks). Obtain documentation and maintain records for compliance. If necessary, adjust product offerings to include only certified models.

quotes.quote: Desktops, laptops, and computer monitors provided under any resulting Agreement are required to have achieved a minimum certification of EPEAT Gold at the time of award with the exception of the three Chromebook Configurations (Chromebook Low, Chromebook with Touchscreen and Chromebook with Touchscreen – 14”). Chromebook Standard Configurations will be required to meet a minimum certification of EPEAT Silver at the time of award.

findings.title: Pricing Must Not Exceed Net NYS Contract Price
findings.fact: Quoted pricing for Standard Configurations and Required Products must not exceed the Net NYS Contract Price on the Manufacturer's Umbrella Contract price list.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must ensure that all quoted prices are at or below the Net NYS Contract Price. Exceeding this price will result in bid rejection. This may impact profit margins and require competitive pricing strategies.
findings.action_recommendation: Review the Manufacturer's Umbrella Contract price list and ensure all proposed pricing is compliant. Develop a pricing strategy that offers competitive discounts while staying within the ceiling. Regularly monitor and adjust pricing to remain compliant throughout the contract term.

quotes.quote: In no event may quoted pricing exceed the Net NYS Contract Price on the Manufacturer’s Umbrella Contract price list.
In no event may quoted pricing exceed the Net NYS Contract Price on the Contractor’s Manufacturer Umbrella Contract.

findings.title: Delivery Period and Notification Deadlines
findings.fact: The Contractor shall deliver units within 45 calendar days of receipt of a Purchase Order, provide a Purchase Order receipt notification within 5 calendar days, and an Advanced Shipping Notice 14 calendar days prior to delivery.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must have robust logistics and order management processes to meet strict delivery and notification deadlines. Failure to comply may result in penalties, contract termination, and damage to reputation.
findings.action_recommendation: Establish internal procedures to ensure timely acknowledgment of purchase orders (within 5 days) and provision of advanced shipping notices (14 days prior). Develop contingency plans to handle potential delays and communicate proactively with Authorized Users. Monitor delivery performance and address any issues promptly.

quotes.quote: The Contractor shall deliver the units ordered by an Authorized User within 45 calendar days of receipt of a Purchase Order, approved by OSC if applicable, unless either the Authorized User or OGS grants an extension of time as provided below.

The Contractor must provide a Purchase Order receipt notification to the Authorized User within five (5) calendar days of receipt of a Purchase Order. An Advanced Shipping Notice must be provided to Authorized Users upon request fourteen (14) calendar days prior to delivery.

findings.title: EOL Notification Deadlines
findings.fact: OGS must receive no less than 60 calendar days notice for EOL Additional Products, and no less than 60 calendar days notice for EOL Products in Standard Configurations/Required Products, and no less than 30 calendar days prior to EOL for substitute Standard Configuration submission.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must proactively monitor product lifecycles and provide timely notifications to OGS to avoid contract non-compliance. Failure to meet these deadlines may result in penalties or loss of contract.
findings.action_recommendation: Implement a product lifecycle management system to track EOL dates and ensure notifications are sent at least 60 days in advance for additional products and standard configurations, and at least 30 days before EOL for substitute configurations. Prepare replacement plans in advance to ensure seamless transitions.

quotes.quote: OGS must receive no less than 60 calendar days notice for EOL Additional Products.
OGS must receive no less than 60 calendar days notice from Contractor for EOL Products, in order for OGS to process modifications for Product substitutions in a timely manner.

No less than 30 calendar days prior to the EOL of the awarded Standard Configuration or the date that the awarded Standard Configuration has become unavailable for purchase by Authorized Users, a substitute Standard Configuration with specifications that meet or exceed the specifications of the original offered Standard Configuration must be submitted for OGS approval by completing the modification process outlined in Appendix 2 – Agreement Price List Modification Procedures.

findings.title: Basis for Award
findings.fact: Awards will be made to the responsive and responsible Contractor(s) with the highest Total Financial Score per Configuration that meets all specified technical requirements. The same Contractor can be awarded multiple Configurations.
findings.business_implication: The award is based on the highest financial score, meaning the lowest price for each configuration, provided technical requirements are met. This emphasizes price competitiveness over other factors. Bidders can win multiple configurations, so a strong pricing strategy across multiple configurations could maximize award opportunities.
findings.action_recommendation: Develop a competitive pricing strategy for each configuration you intend to bid on, ensuring your prices are as low as possible while still meeting technical requirements. Consider bidding on multiple configurations to increase chances of winning, but ensure you can deliver on all awarded configurations.

quotes.quote: Awards will be made to the responsive and responsible Contractor(s) with the highest Total Financial Score per Configuration that meets all the specified technical requirements. The same Contractor can be awarded multiple Configurations.

findings.title: Stage 2 Technical Evaluation
findings.fact: Stage 2 compares Attachment A to Standard Configuration and Required Products requirements. All proposed SKUs must be on the Contractor's approved Manufacturer Umbrella Contract price list. Any configuration with a SKU not on the price list may not proceed further.
findings.business_implication: Technical compliance is a pass/fail gate. If any SKU in your proposed configuration is not on your approved Manufacturer Umbrella Contract price list, your entire configuration will be disqualified from further evaluation. This means you must ensure all products you offer are already listed on your umbrella contract before submission.
findings.action_recommendation: Before submitting, verify that every SKU you plan to offer in Attachment A is on your approved Manufacturer Umbrella Contract price list. If any SKU is missing, either add it to your umbrella contract well in advance or adjust your proposal to include only listed SKUs. Prioritize getting any necessary contract modifications processed before the RFQ deadline.

quotes.quote: Submitted Attachment A – Technical Response will be compared to Standard Configuration and Required Products requirements. All proposed SKUs for proposed products offered in Attachment A – Technical Response must be on the Contractor’s approved Manufacturer Umbrella Contract price list. Any Configuration that contains a SKU that is not included on the Manufacturer’s Umbrella Contract price list may not proceed further in the evaluation process.

findings.title: Stage 3 Financial Evaluation
findings.fact: Only Contractors whose Standard Configuration specifications and Required Products pass review will proceed to evaluation of Attachment C – Financial Response. Attachment C is created from Attachment A and provided to Contractor for completion. Proposed pricing on Attachment C is used in Financial Evaluation.
findings.business_implication: Financial evaluation only occurs after technical pass. Attachment C is generated from your Attachment A, so your technical response directly determines the pricing form you must complete. This means your technical choices will impact your pricing obligations, and you must be prepared to price all items listed in Attachment C.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure your Attachment A is technically compliant and complete, as it will be used to create Attachment C. After submission, be ready to promptly complete Attachment C with competitive pricing for all listed items. Since Attachment C is based on your technical response, avoid including any unnecessary items that could increase your pricing burden.

quotes.quote: Only Contractors whose Standard Configuration specifications and Required Products pass review, as determined by OGS, will proceed to the evaluation of Attachment C – Financial Response for those specific Configurations. For those Contractors who have been determined to have passed the Technical Evaluation, their Attachment A - Technical Response will be used to create the Attachment C – Financial Response and will be provided to the Contractor in order to complete and submit. The proposed pricing on Attachment C – Financial Response will then be used in the Financial Evaluation.

findings.title: Pricing Requirements
findings.fact: All pricing offered on Attachment C - Financial Response must be equal to or better than the pricing offered for that SKU on the Contractor's Manufacturer Umbrella Contract.
findings.business_implication: You cannot inflate prices above your umbrella contract rates. Your bid prices must be at or below the prices you have already established on your Manufacturer Umbrella Contract. This ensures that the state gets at least the same pricing as your contract, and you must offer discounts if you want to be competitive.
findings.action_recommendation: Review your Manufacturer Umbrella Contract pricing for all SKUs you plan to offer. Ensure that your Attachment C pricing is set at or below those contract prices. To be competitive, consider offering discounts off your umbrella contract prices, as the evaluation is based on lowest cost.

quotes.quote: All pricing offered on Attachment C - Financial Response must be equal to or better than the pricing offered for that SKU on the Contractor's Manufacturer Umbrella Contract.

findings.title: Technical Evaluation of Mandatory Specifications
findings.fact: Only items with mandatory specifications are evaluated in the Technical Evaluation; additional items are reviewed only for inclusion in Lot 2 of the Manufacturer Umbrella Contract price list.
findings.business_implication: The technical evaluation focuses only on items with mandatory specifications. Additional items you include to complete a standard configuration are not technically evaluated but must be on your Lot 2 price list. If they are not, they will be removed from your submission, potentially affecting the completeness of your configuration.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure that all additional items you include in Section A of Attachment A are on your Lot 2 price list. If any are missing, either add them to your umbrella contract or remove them from your proposal. Also, focus your technical compliance efforts on the mandatory specification items, as they are the ones that will be evaluated.

quotes.quote: Only items that have a mandatory specification will be evaluated in the Technical Evaluation; additional items needed to create the Standard Configuration listed in Section A of Attachment A- Technical Response will be reviewed only to determine if the items are included in Lot 2 of the Contractor’s Manufacturer Umbrella Contract price list.

findings.title: Required Products Discount Factored into Total Financial Score
findings.fact: The discount percentages bid on Required Products will be factored into the Total Financial Score.
findings.business_implication: Aggressive discounting on Required Products can significantly improve the bidder's Total Financial Score, as these discounts are directly evaluated and weighted (Warranty/Services 15 points, Components 30 points, Peripherals 5 points).
findings.action_recommendation: Bid the most competitive discount percentages possible for Required Products, especially for Components which carry the highest weight (30 points), to maximize the financial score.

quotes.quote: Contractors are encouraged to aggressively discount their pricing for their Required Products, as the pricing will be factored in the Total Financial Score.

findings.title: OGS Reserved Right to Modify Specifications Prior to Financial Evaluation
findings.fact: OGS may modify a specification within the Standard Configuration or Required Product categories prior to the Financial Evaluation, upon written notice.
findings.business_implication: OGS can change the technical requirements after bid submission but before financial evaluation, potentially affecting the bidder's pricing and competitiveness.
findings.action_recommendation: Stay flexible and monitor communications from OGS for any specification changes. Be prepared to adjust pricing or technical offerings accordingly within the given timeframe.

quotes.quote: Modify a specification within the Standard Configuration or Required Product categories in Attachment A – Technical Response or Attachment C – Financial Response prior to the Financial Evaluation, upon written notice to Contractors that have submitted a quote.

findings.title: Discount Percentage Requirements for Required Products
findings.fact: Required Products discount percentages may be increased, but not decreased during the term of any resulting Agreement and any extensions.
findings.business_implication: Once bid, the discount percentages for Required Products are locked in as a floor; the bidder cannot lower them during the contract term, which could impact profitability if costs rise.
findings.action_recommendation: Carefully calculate the minimum viable discount percentages that remain profitable over the long term, considering potential cost increases, and avoid overcommitting to unsustainable discounts.

quotes.quote: The discount percentages may be increased, but not decreased during the term of any resulting Agreement and any extensions.
Required Product discount percentages may be increased, but not decreased during the term of any resulting Agreement and any extensions.

findings.title: Additional Products Discount Application
findings.fact: Contractors shall provide the same awarded discount percentages that applied to the three Required Product categories to the Additional Products in their respective categories.
findings.business_implication: The discount percentages bid for Required Products will automatically apply to all Additional Products in the same category, affecting the bidder's pricing across a broader product range.
findings.action_recommendation: When setting Required Product discounts, consider the impact on Additional Products to ensure overall profitability and competitiveness across the entire product catalog.

quotes.quote: Contractors shall provide the same awarded discount percentages that applied to the three (3) Required Product categories (Warranty and Services, Components, and Peripherals), to the Additional Products in their respective categories.

findings.title: Financial Evaluation Weighting
findings.fact: The Financial Response is 100% of the evaluation, with points weighted as: Standard Configuration 50 points, Required Products (Warranty/Services 15, Components 30, Peripherals 5).
findings.business_implication: The financial proposal is the sole determinant of award, with Standard Configuration pricing carrying the highest weight (50 points), followed by Components (30 points).
findings.action_recommendation: Prioritize competitive pricing on Standard Configurations and Components, as they have the most significant impact on the total financial score. Allocate resources to optimize these areas.

quotes.quote: Financial Response : 100%  Total Financial Score is based on lowest cost and the points are weighted as follows: • Standard Configuration - 50 points • Required Products o Warranty/Services - 15 points o Components - 30 points o Peripherals - 5 points

findings.title: Basis for Award
findings.fact: Awards will be made to the responsive and responsible Contractor(s) with the highest Total Financial Score per Configuration that meets all specified technical requirements.
findings.business_implication: The award is based on the highest financial score, meaning price is the primary factor, but technical compliance is a prerequisite. Bidders must ensure their technical proposal meets all requirements to be considered, and then offer competitive pricing to maximize their financial score.
findings.action_recommendation: Thoroughly review the technical requirements in Attachment A to ensure full compliance. Develop a competitive pricing strategy that optimizes the Total Financial Score, considering all cost components and potential discounts.

quotes.quote: Awards will be made to the responsive and responsible Contractor(s) with the highest Total Financial Score per Configuration that meets all the specified technical requirements.

findings.title: Estimated Spend and Quantity
findings.fact: The estimated dollar value of the aggregated award is approximately $50 million, but there is no guarantee of volume or dollar value to be purchased.
findings.business_implication: While the potential contract value is significant, the actual purchases are uncertain. Bidders should not rely on the estimated volume for capacity planning or revenue projections, as actual orders may be substantially higher or lower.
findings.action_recommendation: Prepare for variable demand by ensuring flexible production and supply chain capabilities. Avoid over-committing resources based on the estimate. Consider pricing strategies that remain competitive even if volumes are lower than expected.

quotes.quote: The estimated dollar value of the aggregated award of the 14 Standard Configurations in this RFQ 23-01, based on historical purchases under previous awards, is approximately $50 million.
There is no guarantee of volume to be purchased
There is no guarantee of dollar value to be purchased

findings.title: Agreement Pricing and Not-To-Exceed
findings.fact: Agreement prices are Not-To-Exceed prices, and off-contract sales are prohibited.
findings.business_implication: The agreed prices are maximum ceilings; bidders cannot charge more than the quoted prices. Additionally, all sales must be made through the contract, limiting flexibility to offer better prices outside the agreement.
findings.action_recommendation: Set prices carefully to ensure they are competitive yet sustainable, as they cannot be increased. Ensure that all sales channels comply with the contract terms to avoid penalties. Consider offering volume discounts within the contract to encourage purchases.

quotes.quote: Agreement prices are Not-To-Exceed prices. Off-Contract sales are prohibited.

findings.title: Warranty Obligations
findings.fact: If a unit becomes inoperable within warranty and cannot be repaired, a brand new unit must be provided at no charge; refurbished or remanufactured equipment is not allowed.
findings.business_implication: This warranty obligation imposes significant replacement costs if units fail irreparably. Bidders must factor in the risk of providing new replacements, including potential data transfer services, which could impact profitability.
findings.action_recommendation: Assess product reliability and historical failure rates to estimate warranty costs. Price the contract to include a warranty reserve. Ensure that the supply chain can support quick replacement of units with new ones, and have processes in place for data transfer if required.

quotes.quote: If a unit becomes inoperable within the warranty window and cannot be repaired, a brand new unit shall be provided at no charge. Contractor shall not provide refurbished or remanufactured equipment as they are not allowed under this Aggregate Hardware Buy 23-01.

findings.title: OGS Not Liable for Preparation Costs
findings.fact: OGS will not be held liable for any cost incurred by the Contractor for work performed in the preparation of a response to this RFQ.
findings.business_implication: Bidders bear all costs associated with preparing and submitting a response, with no reimbursement if they are not awarded. This includes time, resources, and any third-party expenses.
findings.action_recommendation: Budget for bid preparation costs and ensure that the potential contract value justifies the investment. Carefully evaluate the likelihood of winning before committing significant resources. Consider partnering or leveraging existing materials to reduce costs.

quotes.quote: OGS will not be held liable for any cost incurred by the Contractor for work performed in the preparation of a response to this Request for Quote (RFQ).

findings.title: Contractor Assumes Risk for Timely Submission
findings.fact: Contractor assumes all risks for timely, properly submitted RFQ deliveries.
findings.business_implication: The contractor bears the risk of any delays or errors in submission, which could lead to rejection of the bid without recourse.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure a robust submission process with internal deadlines well ahead of the official deadline, and consider using a reliable delivery method with tracking.

quotes.quote: Contractor assumes all risks for timely, properly submitted RFQ deliveries.

findings.title: Contractor Must Furnish All Quantities Ordered
findings.fact: Contractor must furnish all quantities actually ordered by Authorized Users at or below the prices in the Agreement.
findings.business_implication: The contractor is obligated to supply any volume of orders, even if actual demand far exceeds estimates, without the ability to renegotiate prices.
findings.action_recommendation: Assess production and supply chain capacity to handle potential high volumes, and include contingency plans for scaling up.

quotes.quote: Contractor must furnish all quantities actually ordered by Authorized Users at or below the prices in the Aggregate Hardware Buy 23-01 Agreement.

findings.title: Contractor Responsible for Replacement of Incompatible Components
findings.fact: If replacement components are not compatible with Agreement peripherals, the Contractor will be responsible for replacement of both the component and the peripheral.
findings.business_implication: The contractor may incur additional costs if replacement parts are incompatible, potentially leading to financial losses and reputational damage.
findings.action_recommendation: Thoroughly test replacement components for compatibility before offering them, and maintain a list of approved peripherals.

quotes.quote: Replacement components must be compatible with Agreement peripherals or the Contractor will be responsible for replacement of both the component and the peripheral.

findings.title: Contractor Responsible for EOL Products Warranty
findings.fact: All EOL Additional Products, EOL Replacement Products, and EOL Standard Configurations purchased by Authorized Users must remain under warranty or be replaceable at no additional charge to the Authorized Users.
findings.business_implication: The contractor must continue to support end-of-life products, which could lead to increased costs for warranty services or replacements.
findings.action_recommendation: Plan for end-of-life product support by setting aside reserves or negotiating extended warranty terms with manufacturers.

quotes.quote: All EOL Additional Products purchased by Authorized Users must remain under warranty or be replaceable at no additional charge to the Authorized Users.
All EOL Replacement Products purchased by Authorized Users must remain under warranty or be replaceable at no additional charge to the Authorized Users.
All EOL Standard Configurations purchased by Authorized Users must remain under warranty or be replaceable at no additional charge to the Authorized Users.

findings.title: Contractor Responsible for Docking Station Warranty
findings.fact: The Contractor is responsible for providing a warranty SKU(s) for docking stations that fully covers hardware, software, and drivers, and provides complete support including break/fix for all compatible operating systems.
findings.business_implication: The contractor must offer comprehensive warranty coverage for docking stations, which may increase service obligations and costs.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure warranty SKUs are comprehensive and priced to cover potential support costs, and establish a support process for docking stations.

quotes.quote: The Contractor is responsible for providing a warranty SKU(s) for docking stations listed as a Required Product or Additional Product on the price lists. The warranty SKU(s) must fully cover hardware, software, and drivers. The warranty SKU(s) for docking stations must provide complete support, including break/fix, for all compatible operating systems.

findings.title: Contractor Responsible for Additional Product Warranties
findings.fact: The Contractor is responsible for adding SKUs for additional warranty year options under Additional Products.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must ensure that its product catalog includes SKUs for extended warranty options (e.g., 3, 4, 5 years) for all additional products offered. Failure to do so could result in non-compliance with the RFQ requirements, potentially affecting the bid's acceptance or leading to contractual penalties.
findings.action_recommendation: Review the list of additional products in Attachment A and verify that SKUs for all required extended warranty periods are included. If any are missing, add them before submission. Ensure that the pricing for these warranty SKUs is competitive and clearly stated.

quotes.quote: The Contractor is responsible for adding SKUs for additional warranty year options (e.g. 3 year, 4 year, 5 year) under Additional Products on Attachment A – Technical Response.

findings.title: Contractor Solely Responsible for Liability and Performance in Extended Agreements
findings.fact: In the event that the Agreement is extended to other states or governmental jurisdictions, such other authorized entities shall be solely responsible for liability and performance under any resulting Agreement, and Contractor agrees to hold them solely responsible for such liability and performance.
findings.business_implication: This clause limits the bidder's liability when the agreement is extended to other entities, as those entities assume responsibility. However, the bidder must still perform its obligations under the extended agreements and may face risks if those entities fail to meet their responsibilities. The bidder should be aware that it may be held accountable for performance issues even if the other entity is liable.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure that the bidder's legal team reviews this clause to understand the extent of liability. Consider negotiating for clearer indemnification or limitation of liability provisions. Also, establish clear communication channels with any extended entities to mitigate risks.

quotes.quote: In the event that any resulting Agreement is so extended, such other authorized entities shall be solely responsible for liability and performance under any resulting Agreement and Contractor agrees to hold them solely responsible for such liability and performance.

findings.title: Termination for Repeated Failure to Comply
findings.fact: OGS may terminate an Agreement under this RFQ, in whole or in part, for Contractor's repeated failure to comply with any requirement under the Agreement.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must ensure strict compliance with all terms and conditions of the agreement. Repeated failures, even minor ones, could lead to termination, which would result in loss of revenue and potential damage to the bidder's reputation with OGS.
findings.action_recommendation: Implement robust compliance monitoring and internal controls to ensure all requirements are met consistently. Designate a compliance officer to oversee adherence to the agreement. Regularly audit processes to identify and rectify any potential non-compliance issues before they become repeated.

quotes.quote: Terminate an Agreement under this RFQ, in whole or in part, for Contractor’s repeated failure to comply with any requirement under the Agreement.

findings.title: Termination for Delayed Deliveries
findings.fact: If OGS becomes aware of multiple incidents of delays in delivery, OGS reserves the right to enforce remedies including termination of the Agreement in whole or in part, and award to another contractor.
findings.business_implication: Timely delivery is critical. Multiple delays could lead to termination, causing loss of contract and potential financial penalties. The bidder must have a reliable supply chain and logistics plan to meet delivery deadlines consistently.
findings.action_recommendation: Develop a detailed delivery schedule and contingency plans for potential disruptions. Monitor delivery performance closely and address any delays immediately. Maintain open communication with OGS regarding any potential delays and provide proactive updates.

quotes.quote: If OGS becomes aware of multiple incidents of delays in delivery, OGS reserves the right to enforce any of the remedies available to us through the terms of this Agreement, including our rights to terminate the Agreement in whole or in part, and award to another contractor as per the terms of Section 7.22 Replacement Contractor.

findings.title: Termination for Failure to Submit Accurate Sales Reports
findings.fact: Failure to submit accurate sales reports on a timely basis may result in a responsibility hearing and possible termination of the Agreement in whole or in part.
findings.business_implication: Accurate and timely sales reporting is mandatory. Inaccuracies or delays could trigger a responsibility hearing and potential termination, which would be detrimental to the bidder's business. This could also affect the bidder's eligibility for future contracts.
findings.action_recommendation: Establish a robust sales reporting process with clear internal deadlines to ensure reports are submitted on time and accurately. Assign a dedicated team to handle sales reporting and conduct regular audits to ensure data accuracy. Stay updated on reporting requirements and formats.

quotes.quote: Failure to submit accurate reports on a timely basis may result in a responsibility hearing, and possible termination of this Agreement in whole or in part, after which OGS reserves the right to award to another contractor as per the terms of Section 7.22 Replacement Contractor.

findings.title: Termination for Repeated Audit Errors
findings.fact: Repeated errors on subsequent fiscal audits may lead to termination of any resulting Agreement in whole or in part.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must ensure strict accuracy in all sales reporting and audit responses. Repeated errors could result in termination of the agreement, loss of revenue, and potential damage to the bidder's reputation with OGS.
findings.action_recommendation: Implement robust internal controls and review processes for sales reporting. Designate a compliance officer to oversee audit responses and ensure all submissions are accurate and timely. Consider conducting internal audits prior to submission to catch and correct errors.

quotes.quote: Repeated errors on subsequent audits may result in a responsibility hearing in relation to Contractor’s Manufacturer Umbrella Contract and may lead to termination of any resulting Agreement in whole or in part, after which OGS reserves the right to award to another contractor as per the terms of Section 7.22 Replacement Contractor.

findings.title: Conflict in Reseller Participation: RFQ states Resellers are not eligible to respond, but Section 7.10 permits use of Resellers in fulfillment
findings.fact: The RFQ states that Resellers are not eligible to respond and any bids from a Reseller will be disqualified, but later permits Contractors to use Resellers in the fulfillment of orders under any resulting Agreement.
findings.business_implication: This contradiction creates confusion about the role of resellers. The bidder must ensure that its bid is submitted directly as a Lot 2 Contractor, not through a reseller, to avoid disqualification. However, once awarded, the bidder may use resellers for fulfillment, but must remain responsible for all obligations.
findings.action_recommendation: Clarify with OGS the intended interpretation of these provisions. Ensure that the bid is submitted directly by the Contractor entity. If planning to use resellers for fulfillment, document the arrangement and ensure compliance with all requirements, including direct invoicing and payment handling.

quotes.quote: Quotes under RFQ 23-01 will only be accepted from Lot 2 Contractors on the Manufacturer Umbrella Contract; Resellers are not eligible to respond and any bids from a Reseller will be disqualified.
Contractors are permitted to use Resellers in the fulfillment of orders under any resulting Agreement.

findings.title: Conflict in Pricing: Standard Configuration price must remain equal to awarded price, but Contractor may offer lower pricing at any time
findings.fact: Section 6.3.1 states that the awarded Standard Configuration price and its component prices will remain equal to the Agreement awarded price for the term, but also states that Contractor may offer lower pricing at any time, creating ambiguity about whether the price can be lowered.
findings.business_implication: The ambiguity could lead to disputes over pricing flexibility. The bidder needs to understand whether it can lower prices during the contract term without breaching the 'remain equal' requirement. This affects pricing strategy and potential profitability.
findings.action_recommendation: Seek clarification from OGS on the intended interpretation. If lower pricing is permitted, ensure that any price reductions are documented and communicated properly. If not, plan pricing strategy accordingly to avoid non-compliance.

quotes.quote: The awarded Standard Configuration price and its component prices will remain equal to the Agreement awarded price for the term of the Agreement(s) and any extensions, though Contractor may offer lower pricing at any time.
